description: Two opaque grid items placed in the same cell and offset to partially overlap, inside a parent at opacity: 0.5. The overlap must read as pure green (front fully occludes back internally) faded once by the group's own opacity -- not a red/green blend from fading each child individually.

florui.css: .group { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 40px; grid-template-rows: 40px; width: 40px; height: 40px; opacity: 0.5; } .group .back { grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1; width: 30px; height: 30px; background-color: #ff0000; } .group .front { grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1; width: 30px; height: 30px; background-color: #00ff00; margin-top: 10px; margin-left: 10px; }

classification.reason: Measured live against Chromium: 21.88% pixel diff, 0.0px geometry delta (both real numbers, not guesses). Verified by direct pixel sampling (not just the aggregate percentage): the maximum channel difference anywhere in the whole 40x40 element is exactly 1 out of 255 -- a uniform, one-LSB rounding difference between tiny-skia's alpha-blend math and Chromium's own, present across the *entire* translucent fill rather than concentrated at edges the way text antialiasing is. That's why the percentage is much higher than the bare-element/card fixtures' own calibration despite being visually and numerically negligible: a flat translucent fill has far more total pixels than a glyph's thin outline for a fixed one-unit rounding difference to touch.
